newsitem.title: EGYPT: EgyptAir opposes any private competition.
newsitem.headline: EgyptAir opposes any private competition.

text.p: The Egyptian national carrier EgyptAir opposes any competition from private airlines on its routes and is not included in government privatisation plans, the chairman said in an interview published on Thursday.
Chairman Mohamed Fahim Rayyan told the government newspaper al-Ahram that any new private airlines should only take routes EgyptAir has turned down.
A group of Egyptian businessmen have set up a small airline called Cairo Air with a capital of 200 million pounds ($59 million) but the airline has not yet started flying.
It is the first such airline in Egypt since ZAS Airlines of Egypt collapsed in 1995, strangled by exclusion from routes in which it competed with the national carrier.

Rayyan, known for his protectionist views, said: "Private airlines must add something, in other words they should open new markets and keep away from areas where EgyptAir is operating. They can't suddenly come and plant on land which I have reclaimed and on which I have spent lots of money."
He offered to let them take 50 international routes EgyptAir has not taken up -- 20 to African countries, 19 to Asian countries and 11 to European countries.

"The state cannot agree to private airlines which live as parasites on EgyptAir, its efficiency, its resources, its territory and its markets. No one would accept private airlines set up with a mission to compete with EgyptAir," he added.
Government newspapers have previously quoted Rayyan as saying he was preparing EgyptAir for privatisation but on Thursday he said this was not a possibility.

"EgyptAir will not be subject to privatisation. This is what President Hosni Mubarak has said on more than one occasion, that privatisation is not for giant national concerns like EgyptAir and the Suez Canal," he said.
Rayyan also said he opposed any "open skies" agreement covering Egypt for fear big airlines would wipe his company out.
He said the company was negotiating to buy three 50-seat Canadair Regional Jets (CRJ), which are produced by Canada's Bombardier Inc at about $20 million each.
Press reports say EgyptAir made an operating profit of 50.9 million pounds in the financial year 1995/96, which ended on 30 June 1996, against 10.6 million the previous year.
